```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# Self-contained report template for `intrinsix run --report` / pam50_run(report = TRUE).
# It is rendered from a copy in a temp dir (see R/report.R) with the run's
# pam50_result + config passed in via `params`; it re-draws the package's own
# plot functions, so the figures match the saved PDFs exactly.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.align = "center", dev = "png", dpi = 110)
res   <- params$result
cfg   <- params$cfg
calls <- res$calls
n     <- nrow(calls)
has_cluster <- !is.null(res$intrinsic)
call_col <- if (!is.null(calls$Call_CLOW)) "Call_CLOW" else "Call"
```

This report summarises a PAM50 intrinsic-subtyping run produced by the
[**intrinsix**](https://github.com/swarbricklab/intrinsix) R package. It is
self-contained: all figures and tables are embedded, so it can be shared as a
single file.

## What PAM50 subtyping is

PAM50 assigns each breast-tumour expression profile to one of **five intrinsic
molecular subtypes** — **Luminal A (LumA)**, **Luminal B (LumB)**,
**HER2-enriched (Her2)**, **Basal-like (Basal)**, and **Normal-like (Normal)** —
by comparing the sample's expression of 50 signature genes to five published
reference *centroids* (Parker, Perou *et al.*, *J Clin Oncol* 2009). The sample
is called as the subtype whose centroid it is **most correlated** with (Spearman
rank correlation). From the same correlations the method derives the **ROR**
(Risk Of Recurrence) scores. When intrinsic clustering is enabled, a
**claudin-low (CLOW)** group can additionally be identified.

Each call is a *relative* assignment to the nearest of five profiles — read it
together with the per-subtype correlations and the confidence value below, not
in isolation.

## Run overview

```{r overview}
params_tbl <- data.frame(
  Setting = c("Samples classified",
              "Zhao4 normalisation",
              "Calibration",
              "Duplicate-gene collapse",
              "Intrinsic clustering / claudin-low"),
  Value = c(
    n,
    if (isTRUE(res$params$zhao)) "on" else "off",
    as.character(res$params$calibration),
    res$params$collapse,
    if (has_cluster) "on" else "off"
  ),
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(params_tbl, caption = "Run configuration.")
```

### Subtype distribution

```{r distribution}
tab <- as.data.frame(table(Subtype = calls[[call_col]]), responseName = "Samples")
tab$`% of cohort` <- round(100 * tab$Samples / sum(tab$Samples), 1)
knitr::kable(tab, caption = sprintf("Number of samples per call (column: %s).", call_col))
```

```{r distribution-bar, fig.width=6, fig.height=4, fig.cap="Subtype call counts across the cohort."}
op <- graphics::par(mar = c(5, 4, 2, 1))
cols <- c(Basal = "red", Her2 = "hotpink", LumA = "darkblue",
          LumB = "skyblue", Normal = "forestgreen", CLOW = "orange")
bp <- table(calls[[call_col]])
graphics::barplot(bp, col = cols[names(bp)], ylab = "Samples",
                  main = "", las = 1)
graphics::par(op)
```

## Visualisations

### Per-subtype centroid correlations

The six panels below (one per subtype, plus the proliferation index) show, for
each predicted call, the distribution of that sample group's **correlation to
every subtype centroid**. A clean classification shows each group peaking on its
*own* centroid panel and sitting lower on the others; overlap between groups
flags samples whose call is less clear-cut. The final panel is the
**proliferation index** (mean standardised expression of the proliferation
genes), which rises from LumA through LumB/Her2/Basal and underlies the ROR-P
score.

```{r scores-plot, fig.width=9, fig.height=10, fig.cap="Per-subtype centroid-correlation boxplots (samples grouped by predicted call) and the proliferation index."}
ok <- tryCatch({ intrinsix::plot_pam50_scores(res); TRUE },
               error = function(e) { message("score plot failed: ", conditionMessage(e)); FALSE })
```

```{r scores-plot-note, results="asis"}
if (!exists("ok") || !isTRUE(ok)) cat("*Score-distribution plot could not be drawn for this run.*\n")
```

### Training + test PCA

The three PCA panels place the classified samples against the published PAM50
**training set**: coloured by cohort (train vs this run), by the training
samples' known subtypes, and by the predicted calls for this run. They show
whether the cohort occupies the same expression space as the reference and
whether the calls fall where the corresponding training subtypes sit.

```{r pca-plot, fig.width=12, fig.height=4.5, fig.cap="PCA of the training set plus this run's samples: by cohort, by training subtype, and by predicted call."}
ok_pca <- tryCatch({ intrinsix::plot_pam50_pca(res); TRUE },
                   error = function(e) { message("PCA plot failed: ", conditionMessage(e)); FALSE })
```

```{r pca-plot-note, results="asis"}
if (!exists("ok_pca") || !isTRUE(ok_pca)) cat("*PCA plot could not be drawn for this run (e.g. too few overlapping genes).*\n")
```

```{r cluster-section, eval=has_cluster, results="asis"}
cat("### Intrinsic-subtype heatmap and claudin-low\n\n")
cat("Intrinsic clustering was enabled. The heatmap shows median-centred",
    "expression of the intrinsic gene set (genes x samples), annotated with the",
    "claudin-low-adjusted call and the silhouette sign. The silhouette plot",
    "quantifies how well each sample fits its assigned cluster (1 - Pearson",
    "distance): positive widths indicate a good fit, negative widths a sample",
    "that sits closer to another group.\n\n")
cat(sprintf("**Claudin-low samples identified: %d.**\n\n",
            length(res$intrinsic$claudin_low)))
```

```{r heatmap, eval=has_cluster, fig.width=10, fig.height=7, fig.cap="Median-centred intrinsic-gene expression heatmap (blue = low, yellow = high)."}
if (requireNamespace("ComplexHeatmap", quietly = TRUE) &&
    requireNamespace("circlize", quietly = TRUE)) {
  clow <- res$intrinsic$claudin_low
  ann <- data.frame(
    Call_CLOW = calls[colnames(res$intrinsic$int_medctr), "Call_CLOW"],
    check.names = FALSE
  )
  rownames(ann) <- colnames(res$intrinsic$int_medctr)
  if (!is.null(calls$silhouette_width)) {
    ann$sil_width_bin <- ifelse(
      calls[rownames(ann), "silhouette_width"] < 0, "Negative", "Positive")
  }
  hm <- tryCatch(
    intrinsix::pam50_heatmap(res$intrinsic$int_medctr, annotations = ann,
                             title = sprintf("Intrinsic subtype heatmap (n=%d)",
                                             ncol(res$intrinsic$int_medctr))),
    error = function(e) { message("heatmap failed: ", conditionMessage(e)); NULL })
  if (!is.null(hm)) ComplexHeatmap::draw(hm)
} else {
  message("ComplexHeatmap/circlize not installed; skipping heatmap.")
}
```

```{r silhouette, eval=has_cluster, fig.width=9, fig.height=7, fig.cap="Silhouette widths per sample, grouped by claudin-low-adjusted call."}
if (!is.null(res$intrinsic$silhouette)) {
  graphics::plot(res$intrinsic$silhouette, border = NA)
  graphics::abline(v = 0)
}
```

## Results table

One row per sample with its call and the underlying scores. Column meanings:

- **Basal / Her2 / LumA / LumB / Normal** — Spearman correlation of the sample to
  each subtype centroid (higher = more similar).
- **Call** — the assigned subtype (the centroid with the highest correlation).
- **Confidence** — `1 - p` of the Spearman correlation test between the sample and
  its assigned centroid; values near **1** indicate a confident call, lower values
  a weaker fit.
- **ROR-S (Subtype Only)** / **ROR-P (Subtype + Proliferation)** — Risk Of
  Recurrence scores (0-100), with their **low / med / high** group columns.
- **Proliferation Score** — mean standardised expression of the proliferation
  genes.
- **ER / Her2** — standardised expression of `ESR1` / `ERBB2`.
```{r table-extra-cols, results="asis"}
if (!is.null(calls$Call_CLOW)) cat("- **Call_CLOW** — the call after claudin-low reassignment.\n")
if (!is.null(calls$silhouette_width)) cat("- **silhouette_width** — cluster-fit width (positive = good fit).\n")
```

```{r results-table}
disp <- data.frame(Sample = rownames(calls), calls, check.names = FALSE,
                   row.names = NULL)
# round any numeric-looking columns for display
num_cols <- setdiff(names(disp), "Sample")
for (cc in num_cols) {
  v <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(disp[[cc]]))
  if (!all(is.na(v))) disp[[cc]] <- ifelse(is.na(v), disp[[cc]], format(round(v, 3)))
}
knitr::kable(disp, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = sprintf("Per-sample PAM50 calls and scores (n = %d).", n))
```

## Caveats

- PAM50 is a **single-sample, relative** classifier: every sample is forced into
  the nearest of five (or six, with claudin-low) reference profiles. A call with
  low confidence or overlapping centroid correlations should be treated with
  caution.
- Results depend on the input being appropriately **normalised** (log2-scale;
  Zhao4 subtype-specific centering when enabled) and on the **gene set matching**
  the classifier — gene-symbol drift can silently drop signature genes, so prefer
  the ID-based selection paths where possible.
- Centroid correlations are computed on the 50 PAM50 genes; the intrinsic
  heatmap/clustering uses the larger intrinsic gene set.
- This report presents the run as-is; it does not re-run or alter the
  classification. The authoritative outputs are the TSV/`.txt` files written
  alongside it.
